description: issue #953, the second half of the rule #1034 made normative: "Charging a tick does not create an additional step or `instruction` event" (spec/interaction-events.md, `### wait <n>`). Charging each tick against the execution budget could plausibly have been implemented by emitting a per-tick `instruction` event -- that is what every other charged unit in the language that a learner can step through does -- and this fixture is what STATES the rule. It is not the only thing that would notice an unconditional per-tick emission: wait-basic already folds `wait 2` to two events, and measured, 46 fixtures fail under that mutation. What this one adds is scale and intent -- 300 ticks folding to exactly TWO events, the statement's own `instruction` plus the trailing `primitive` the completed pause emits, where a per-tick emission would record 301. 300 is the tick count spec/examples/10-game.logo itself holds open with, so the case pinned here is the canonical one rather than a contrived scale. Why it matters to a learner, and not merely to the trace: a step is defined as "the span from one `instruction` event to the next" (spec/execution-model.md#trace-and-event-registry), so `instruction` events ARE the stepper's units -- under that mutation, pressing Next step on `wait 300` would have cost 301 presses instead of one, and the studio's step control would have become unusable on the spec's own game example. The budget has never counted `instruction` events (a `repeat` pass is charged without emitting one; measured, `repeat 300 [ ]` and `repeat 5000 [ ]` each emit exactly one), so charging a tick without emitting one introduces no new divergence between what the budget counts and what the stepper steps. A conformance fixture can only pin one n, and an implementation emitting per-tick only PAST some threshold passes every fixture below it -- measured at a threshold of 1000, all 942 fixtures including this one still pass. Constancy in n is therefore pinned separately by packages/runtime/src/interaction-wait.test.mjs across n = 0, 1, 2, 300, 5000 and 200000, with `repeat n` as the instrument's positive control there; the two are complements and neither alone is sufficient.
